title: latency-waterfall-and-log-context-correlation
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: We've seen intermittent long-tail latency that isn't captured well by existing per-request percentiles because cost is distributed across phases (ingest/queue, tokenizer, kv-lookup, decode, scheduling). This PR introduces per-token latency decomposition metrics, a waterfall dashboard, and log context propagation so on-callers can quickly correlate traces, logs, and metrics for a single long request.

Summary of changes: added a lightweight exporter that emits redwood.latency.decomp.{phase} (histograms and p50/p90/p99 counters) keyed by model, route, customer_tier, and token_bucket; propagated a stable token_span_id through the request path and enriched structured logs with it; added a Grafana waterfall dashboard for per-request breakdowns and a composite alert tuned to reduce noisy host-triggered incidents.

Checklist: [x] Add metrics and histograms to serving runtime (Go) [x] Propagate token_span_id in trace context (Python + Go) [x] Dashboard + example runbook [x] Integration tests that synthesize long-tail requests [x] Alert tuning and documentation link

Implementation notes: the exporter lives in platform/observability and exposes per-request rollups as histogram buckets (we chose expo-aligned buckets after benchmarking against production token distributions). For memory/speed reasons we compute the phase deltas in runtime hot-path and emit a small proto to the exporter. The token_span_id is derived deterministically from request_id + token_index (64-bit) to allow deterministic correlation without persisting state; it is attached to OpenTelemetry trace attributes and to our structured logs via the new propagator.

Backward compatibility and rollout: the metric names are additive (no renames). The propagator is a no-op unless the head_branch sets the feature flag in config (default off) and is guarded in code paths to ensure zero impact if not enabled. Rollout was performed as a canary: 5% traffic for 48h, then 25% for 24h, then full. We used the existing routing policy to fallback automatically to token_span_id-less logs if the propagator wasn't available.

Dashboard and alerting: added web/console/dashboards/latency-waterfall.json which contains a waterfall panel that assembles phase histograms for a single request using the token_span_id as join key. The SLO alert in slo/alerting/late_tail_rules.yaml uses a composite rule: it fires only when both (a) cluster-level tail latency p99 > threshold and (b) >10% of affected requests show decode-time > queue-time to reduce noisy host false positives. We also added a suppression rule for noisy hosts (nodes with known tracebacks) and tuned the Alertmanager grouping.

Testing: integration-tests/observability/test_latency_decomp.py adds synthetic traces that assert decomposition sums approximately to total latency, validates token_span_id appears in logs and traces, and checks the dashboard query can join metrics and logs for a single span. CI: two flakes were hit during first run (flaky histogram bucket assertion) and fixed by relaxing the test tolerance and improving retry logic.

Security/Privacy: token_span_id is not PII; it is an opaque numeric derived deterministically and logged only when feature flag enabled. Documentation: docs/observability/latency_decomp.md explains metric names, recommended dashboard queries, and a playbook for debugging long-tail incidents.

Rollout notes for on-call: the playbook highlights common patterns (kv-lookup spikes vs decode CPU saturation) and how to use the waterfall panel to triage. We also included an example alert edit to reduce noisy host signatures.

Links: Linear ENG-8421 (latency decomposition), support ticket SUP-3210 for customer incident referenced in motivation.

review_comments:
Miguel Torres (2026-02-13): Can we avoid extra allocations in hot-path when the feature flag is off? Aisha: the token_span_id path is guarded and allocation-free in the fast path; added benchmarks and micro-optimization to avoid allocs.

Tom Becker (2026-02-15): Alert composite seems complex; will this increase MTTR? Aisha: composite reduces noisy host false positives by correlating decode-heavy requests; included simulated incident in test suite and updated playbook to guide responders.
